title: European Ethical Charter on the use of artificial intelligence in judicial systems and their environment
issuer: European Commission for the Efficiency of Justice (CEPEJ), Council of Europe
description: Five principles for AI in judicial systems, used by courts across Europe as a test of a tool and its deployment.

requirements.title: Respect for fundamental rights
requirements.text: The tool's design and use are compatible with fundamental rights, including access to a judge and a fair trial.

requirements.title: Non-discrimination
requirements.text: No conclusion is drawn from a person's membership of a group.
requirements.instruction: Draw no conclusion from a person's membership of a group or from characteristics such as origin, sex, age or social status.

requirements.title: Quality and security
requirements.text: Sources are certified, data is not altered, and the environment is secure.

requirements.title: Transparency, impartiality and fairness
requirements.text: How the output was produced can be inspected, and nothing is hidden from the parties' scrutiny.

requirements.title: Under user control
requirements.text: Users remain informed actors in control of their choices and can depart from anything the tool produces.
